detail.readme: Go-app is a package for **building progressive web apps (PWAs)** with [Go](https://go.dev) and [WebAssembly (Wasm)](https://webassembly.org). Write your UI in Go using **reusable components** and a [declarative syntax](https://go-app.dev/declarative-syntax). Handle user interactions in Go and serve your app with the standard [`net/http`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http) package. Apps built with go-app are **SEO-friendly** and support **offline use**. On supported browsers and devices, users can **install your app and run it in its own window**. ## Documentation (built with go-app) [![go-app documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maxence-charriere/go-app-docs/main/docs/web/images/go-app.png)](https://go-app.dev) ## Install Requires [Go 1.26 or newer](https://go.dev/dl/). From your project directory, initialize a Go module if you do not already have one. Replace `example.com/myapp` with your module path: ```sh go mod init example.com/myapp ``` Add go-app to your project: ```sh go get github.com/maxence-charriere/go-app/v11/pkg/app ``` ## Components Describe your UI with Go functions using go-app's [declarative syntax](https://go-app.dev/declarative-syntax). Each component embeds `app.Compo` and defines a `Render` method that returns its UI. Create a `main.go` file with the following component, then add the `main` function from the next section. The component displays a greeting that updates as you type your name: ```go package main import ( "log" "net/http" "github.com/maxence-charriere/go-app/v11/pkg/app" ) type hello struct { app.Compo name string } func (h *hello) Render() app.UI { return app.Div().Body( app.H1().Body( app.Text("Hello, "), app.If(h.name != "", func() app.UI { return app.Text(h.name) }).Else(func() app.UI { return app.Text("World!") }), ), app.Input(). Type("text"). Value(h.name). Placeholder("What is your name?"). AutoFocus(true). OnInput(h.ValueTo(&h.name)), ) } ``` ## Serving the app Serve your app with Go's standard [`net/http`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http) package. The `app.Handler` type implements `http.Handler` and can be used with an existing Go server. Add this function to `main.go` to register the component at `/` and serve the app on port `8000`: ```go func main() { // Register the component. app.Route("/", func() app.Composer { return &hello{} }) // Start the app in the browser; on the server, continue below. app.RunWhenOnBrowser() // Serve the app over HTTP. http.Handle("/", &app.Handler{ Name: "Hello", Description: "A Hello World example", }) if err := http.ListenAndServe(":8000", nil); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } } ``` ## Build and run From your project directory, build the WebAssembly app and the server, then run the server: ```sh mkdir -p web GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -o web/app.wasm go build -o server ./server ``` Open [localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000) in your browser. After changing the code, rebuild both binaries and restart the server. ## Getting started Follow the [Getting Started guide](https://go-app.dev/getting-started) to build and run your first app. ## Built with go-app - [Murlok](https://murlok.io/): World of Warcraft character builds and guides. - [GoApp Docs](https://go-app.dev/): The documentation website, built with go-app. - [liwasc](https://pojntfx.github.io/liwasc/): Network discovery, port scanning, and Wake-on-LAN. ## Support the project If go-app is useful to you, consider [sponsoring its development](https://github.com/sponsors/maxence-charriere).
